assessmentType: AI web review; no listening grades
rules: Evaluate the original literal prompt using the identical baseline rubric. Frozen-input parser errors remain part of the control limitation, not an excuse to change the rubric.

Review every returned occurrence with exact recording/version identity, independent source applicability, and explicit unsupported facets. Imported tags and engine fit labels are not independent truth.
Reuse prior web findings only after checking exact identity and rubric applicability. Preserve sources, retrieval attempts and version uncertainty.
Hide engine fit labels until the musical verdict where practical. These controls are not a fully blinded human study; reviewers may recognize previously reviewed recordings.
Retain all eight selected cases and 80 requested slots per arm. Ineligible input, runtime failure, zero output, unaudited output and unknown musical fit are distinct.
Compare B5 versus T5 for common-input/common-cap generation; T5 versus T10 for added budget. Live sources, host caches and fixed exploratory selection limit attribution.
Report playlist coverage, hard violations, version uncertainty, concentration and transitions separately from returned-track verdicts; do not invent listening judgments.

rubrics.prompt: Make a 10-track instrumental playlist for focused work, blending modern classical, ambient, and gentle electronic music. Start sparse, build a subtle pulse in the middle, and finish calmly. No vocals.
criteria: no vocals anywhere in each selected recording
modern-classical, ambient and gentle-electronic blend
sparse opening
subtle rhythmic pulse in the middle
calm ending
suitable concentration-oriented dynamics
interpretationNotes: No vocals is an essential exclusion; lyrics, vocal credits, spoken voice or sung samples contradict it, even if most of the track is instrumental.
An instrumental tag or a voice-free preview cannot establish absence across the full recording.
The sparse-to-pulse-to-calm arc and all three musical families are playlist properties.
